page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v5 is a general-purpose server instance from the DDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance includes 1843 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and does not feature any GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks place this instance consistently in the average tier for most workloads. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1630.0 and a multi-core score of 15064.0. Cryptographic and image processing capabilities are notable strengths, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring 43321.1 and Geekbench image processing reaching 14001.0, both ranking in the top 25%. However, memory bandwidth drops to 156.5 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and text generation for large 70B LLM models is a performance bottleneck, registering a weak 2.74 tokens/sec.

The inclusion of 1843 GB of local storage alongside a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides solid resource density for general-purpose workloads. This makes the D48ds_v5 qualitatively cost-efficient for applications requiring fast local scratch space without the overhead of external storage attachments. It is well-suited for relational databases, static web serving, software compilation, and medium-scale text or image processing pipelines.
description: The Microsoft Azure D48ds_v5 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with 48 dedicated vCPUs, 24 physical cores, and 192.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 1843 GB of local SSD storage but lacks GPU acceleration. Benchmark data indicates average overall performance, with a Passmark CPU score of 48717.7 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 15064.0. It shows strong performance in CPU encryption and image processing, though it exhibits weak throughput on large-scale LLM text generation. With a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core and a 2.8 GHz clock speed, the hardware configuration supports diverse workloads. It delivers a static web serving throughput of 38.67 GB/sec and handles 42.89 million Redis SET operations per second, representing a reliable option for enterprise applications requiring local storage.
